Other tidbits:
- The oscillation in "wrongness" on the top boundary in the lower image is related to the edges and centers of the cells. The effective sum of these vectors seems to respect mass conservation.
- The error does not get appreciably smaller with increasing mesh refinement
Make sure to check AMG and GMG as they have different implementations regarding mesh deformation and boundary conditions in general.
And I would trust AMG more. 😀
@tjhei these tests have the same problems both for AMG and GMG, we are concentrating on AMG during testing.

The problem appears with both solvers (we started with AMG), but their results are slightly different. Here is one more interesting data point. I have run the test that Bob linked above one time with mesh deformation, and one time with a prescribed initial topography that is identical to the final state of the mesh deformation plugin, but without activated mesh deformation (i.e. the mesh is deformed initially, but never changed). The model with initial topography does not show the described problems. The plot below shows the end point of the model with a few code modifications I will put into a PR. Top boundary is always no normal flux (=tangential flux = free slip). The top row is the model using initial topography, this is exactly what we would expect, the middle row shows mesh deformation with GMG, the bottom row mesh deformation with AMG. I think this illustrates the problem pretty nicely. The only difference from an ASPECT point of view that I can think of is that we are using a different mapping for the mesh deformation cases (`MappingQEulerian(1)` vs `MappingQ1`). Maybe we need to start digging into the deal.II mappings?
See #6819 for my code changes that give the state I posted above.
Either the mapping is not returning the correct normals or we are somehow accounting twice for the deformation (does the mesh velocity need to be normal to the undeformed Mesh?!)

@tjhei I did wonder about whether we are double counting deformation in mine/@gassmoeller branches, but the pattern made me think it was something else. Do you think that double counting can explain why the vertices and edges of the deformed mesh boundary have different velocities?

> Do you think that double counting can explain why the vertices and edges of the deformed mesh boundary have different velocities?

Yes and I think we are doing things fundamentally wrong:
We compute a finite element vector ``mesh_displacements`` in mesh_deformation/interface.cc which determines the deformation from the reference frame to the deformed mesh. This means the displacement is defined in the reference frame and not in the deformed frame. But we incorrectly assemble/solve/update it using the current mapping (which already contains the current displacement). That seems wrong.
@bobmyhill @gassmoeller @bangerth do you agree that we need to solve for the displacement and displacement updates on the mesh in the reference configuration?

@tjhei the mesh deformation itself looks correct (at least for `tests/function_mesh_deformation_tangential_mesh_velocity.prm` and also`tests/hill_diffusion.prm`). It's the update to the normals that is problematic. I agree with you that the way we update the constraints looks wrong, and that it might be the mapping that is incorrect. I did start to dig into the code over the Christmas break to try to understand the structure better, but I didn't get very far.

Bob, compute_no_normal_flux_constraints() has an optional bool argument (defaulting to true) for the normals: https://dealii.org/current/doxygen/deal.II/group__constraints.html#gaa1a10a9bc3b10deb7543fef6ed0470cb

Could you try setting it to false and see if it makes a difference?

> Bob, compute_no_normal_flux_constraints() has an optional bool argument (defaulting to true) for the normals: https://dealii.org/current/doxygen/deal.II/group__constraints.html#gaa1a10a9bc3b10deb7543fef6ed0470cb
> 
> Could you try setting it to false and see if it makes a difference?

If this is set to true, we ask the manifold here: 
https://github.com/dealii/dealii/blob/master/include/deal.II/numerics/vector_tools_constraints.templates.h#L750

But we have a ``FlatManifold`` and I am not exactly sure what it does for the normals. :-)

@tjhei I made the changes to both `compute_no_normal_flux_constraints_on_level()` and `compute_no_normal_flux_constraints` in - `./source/mesh_deformation/interface.cc` - `./source/simulator/core.cc` - `./source/simulator/solver/stokes_matrix_free_global_coarsening.cc` - `./source/simulator/solver/stokes_matrix_free_local_smoothing.cc` i.e. adding `/*use_manifold_for_normal=*/` `false` Here are the results for `tests/function_mesh_deformation_tangential_mesh_velocity_simple_shear.prm`: Block AMG: Block GMG: The AMG result looks like what I expect (hooray!!!). The GMG result has flow tangential to the boundary of the domain (also hooray!!), but the result is clearly different to the AMG result, and specifically it still has a discontinuity in flow at timestep zero (harroo). I also tried the same thing but with `/*use_manifold_for_normal=*/` `true` in `compute_no_normal_flux_constraints_on_level()` (which appears only in `compute_mesh_displacements_gmg()` in the file `mesh_deformation/interface.cc` and `setup_dofs()` in the file `simulator/solver/stokes_matrix_free_local_smoothing.cc`). This does not appear to change the result from what I have shown above.

> compute_no_normal_flux_constraints_on_level()

This should also use ``false``. I suspect a different problem (displacement not being updated correctly or something like that).  We have to manually "refresh" the deformation, see here:
https://github.com/geodynamics/aspect/blob/83f5ea33ae078681ccf34602155d5bba4d3d5fbc/source/simulator/solver/stokes_matrix_free_local_smoothing.cc#L161-L162

We might need to do this before computing the constraints...

could you try adding the "update_mapping" code from above right before https://github.com/geodynamics/aspect/blob/83f5ea33ae078681ccf34602155d5bba4d3d5fbc/source/simulator/solver/stokes_matrix_free_local_smoothing.cc#L1618 ?
@tjhei I gave it a try and reran the test with the GMG solver. Identical result, at least to the naked eye.

Thank you for checking. I will need to play with it when I have some more time.
It would be worth making a PR for the AMG fix already.
Thanks @tjhei, I've raised a PR in @gassmoeller's repo (https://github.com/gassmoeller/aspect/pull/24) so that he can have a look and suggest any more changes.
